skill.name: pyhealth
skill.description: Guides PyHealth workflows for healthcare machine learning with EHR data, medical codes, physiological signals, clinical tasks, model selection, training, and evaluation.
skill.summary: Build and evaluate healthcare machine learning workflows with PyHealth.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: All static findings appear to be false positives caused by Markdown code fences, inline backticks, visible installation examples, medical terminology, and documentation links. I found no prompt injection text, hidden execution path, data exfiltration intent, or autonomous network behavior in the reviewed files.

remediation.suggestion: Keep code examples fenced and clearly label them as user-run examples. Avoid inline backticks around prose when plain text is sufficient.

remediation.issue: Installation guidance includes a shell command.
remediation.suggestion: State that users should review package installation commands before running them and pin versions when reproducibility matters.

remediation.issue: Healthcare workflows can involve sensitive clinical data.
remediation.suggestion: Add an explicit reminder to use de-identified data and follow local privacy, security, and clinical validation requirements.

content.value_statement: Clinical machine learning projects require careful handling of datasets, coding systems, tasks, models, and validation. This skill organizes PyHealth guidance so Claude, Codex, and Claude Code can help design reproducible healthcare AI workflows.
actual_capabilities: Explains PyHealth dataset loading for EHR, signal, image, and text data.
Guides clinical prediction tasks such as mortality, readmission, drug recommendation, and sleep staging.
Compares PyHealth model families including RETAIN, SafeDrug, GAMENet, Transformer, CNN, RNN, and GNN models.
Describes preprocessing patterns for sequences, labels, labs, physiological signals, clinical text, and images.
Covers training, evaluation, calibration, fairness checks, uncertainty, and interpretability for clinical models.
Provides reference guidance for ICD, NDC, RxNorm, ATC, CCS, and related medical coding workflows.
limitations: It provides documentation guidance and examples, not access to protected clinical datasets.
It does not validate a model for clinical deployment or regulatory approval.
It does not replace review by clinicians, privacy officers, or security teams.
Examples may need updates for local PyHealth versions, dataset schemas, and compute limits.

use_cases.title: Design an ICU Mortality Model
use_cases.description: Plan a PyHealth workflow that loads MIMIC data, defines a mortality task, selects an interpretable model, and evaluates clinical metrics.

use_cases.title: Standardize Medical Codes
use_cases.description: Map diagnosis, procedure, and medication codes across ICD, CCS, NDC, RxNorm, and ATC systems for consistent features.

use_cases.title: Review Deployment Readiness
use_cases.description: Check calibration, fairness, uncertainty, interpretability, and external validation needs before a healthcare model is piloted.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Dataset and Task
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning a clinical prediction project.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the PyHealth skill to help me choose a dataset and predefined task for predicting 30-day readmission. Explain the required inputs, labels, and train validation test split.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Baseline Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate user creating a first reproducible pipeline.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the PyHealth skill to outline a baseline mortality prediction workflow with MIMIC-IV, patient-level splits, preprocessing, a simple model, and suitable evaluation metrics.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Healthcare Models
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the PyHealth skill to compare RETAIN, Transformer, SafeDrug, and GAMENet for a medication recommendation project. Include data needs, interpretability, and evaluation tradeoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Clinical ML Readiness
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced user preparing a model for review.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the PyHealth skill to review a trained clinical model plan for leakage risks, calibration, fairness, uncertainty, external validation, privacy controls, and deployment gaps.

output_examples.input: Plan a PyHealth workflow for ICU mortality prediction.
output_examples.output: The skill would outline dataset loading, mortality task setup, patient-level splitting, RETAIN or Transformer selection, AUPRC-focused evaluation, calibration, and interpretation steps.

output_examples.input: Help me standardize medication codes for drug safety analysis.
output_examples.output: The skill would describe how to map medication codes through supported vocabularies, choose an ATC level, handle one-to-many mappings, and document code versions.

output_examples.input: Review whether my clinical model is ready for deployment.
output_examples.output: The skill would check held-out testing, external validation, demographic fairness, calibration quality, uncertainty estimates, privacy controls, and clinician review requirements.

best_practices: Split data by patient to reduce leakage between training, validation, and test sets.
Match metrics to the clinical task, class balance, and model use case.
Validate models with clinicians and external data before any clinical use.
anti_patterns: Do not treat public benchmark performance as proof of clinical safety.
Do not train on protected health information without approved privacy controls.
Do not compare models without consistent preprocessing, splits, and metrics.

faq.question: Does this skill include clinical datasets?
faq.answer: No. It explains how PyHealth works with supported datasets, but users must obtain and manage datasets separately.

faq.question: Can it help with MIMIC-IV projects?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for loading MIMIC-IV, defining tasks, splitting data, training models, and evaluating results.

faq.question: Does it support medical code mapping?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers PyHealth guidance for ICD, CCS, NDC, RxNorm, ATC, and related mapping workflows.

faq.question: Can it replace clinical validation?
faq.answer: No. It helps structure model development, but clinical validation and governance remain required.

faq.question: Which assistants can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Is the skill only for deep learning?
faq.answer: No. It also covers baselines, preprocessing, evaluation, calibration, fairness, and interpretability.
